summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would expand oversight by the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security and Parliament's intelligence committee, and introduce limited immunity for defence cyber activities.
Oversight would extend to four additional agencies, while the parliamentary committee could initiate certain legislative reviews and ask the Inspector-General to conduct inquiries.

The cyber immunity would cover authorised defence activities undertaken with a reasonable belief that their computer-related effects would occur outside Australia, including mistaken location assessments.
changes: Oversight would cover the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission and intelligence functions of federal police, the financial intelligence agency and Home Affairs.
The parliamentary intelligence committee could review proposed national security reforms and expiring national security legislation on its own initiative.
The Inspector-General and national intelligence head would have to brief the parliamentary intelligence committee annually.
Secrecy law exceptions would permit relevant disclosures to officials carrying out intelligence oversight duties.
summary.affected: Intelligence agencies, oversight bodies, defence officials, complainants and people whose information is held by those agencies are affected.
